evals.prompt:
Draw me the architecture of this application as a diagram. Do it inline here, no need to delegate to an agent. The project is a small Flask app, here is everything the code does:

- app/__init__.py: create_app() factory, registers blueprints auth_bp (routes/auth.py) and deals_bp (routes/deals.py)
- app/models.py: SQLAlchemy models User, Company, Deal stored in PostgreSQL
- app/services/billing.py: calls the external Stripe API to create invoices
- app/templates/: Jinja2 templates rendered by the blueprints
- docker-compose.yml: services web (gunicorn) and db (postgres:16)
evals.expected_output: C4 container diagram as native mxGraph XML for a .drawio file, with the real component names and layer colors
expectations: The answer contains native mxGraph XML (an <mxGraphModel> element), not Mermaid or PlantUML
The diagram uses the real names from the description: auth_bp, deals_bp, PostgreSQL and Stripe
The data layer (models, PostgreSQL) is filled with the light blue #dae8fc
The external Stripe API is filled with the light red #f8cecc
The route blueprints are filled with the light green #d5e8d4
The generated XML contains no XML comments (<!-- -->)

evals.prompt:
Create an ERD for this project's database, inline please, no agent. These are the models:

class Company(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    name = db.Column(db.String(120), nullable=False)

class User(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    email = db.Column(db.String(255), unique=True, nullable=False)
    company_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('company.id'))

class Deal(db.Model):
    id = db.Column(db.Integer, primary_key=True)
    title = db.Column(db.String(200), nullable=False)
    amount = db.Column(db.Numeric(10, 2))
    owner_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('user.id'))
    company_id = db.Column(db.Integer, db.ForeignKey('company.id'))
evals.expected_output: ERD as native mxGraph XML with tables, columns, PK/FK markers and relationship cardinality
expectations: The answer contains native mxGraph XML (an <mxGraphModel> element), not Mermaid or PlantUML
The diagram has the three tables Company, User and Deal with their columns
Primary keys and foreign keys are marked, for example PK and FK labels
The foreign keys user.company_id, deal.owner_id and deal.company_id are drawn as relationships
Relationships carry cardinality labels such as 1, N or 1:N
The tables are filled with the Data layer color light blue #dae8fc

evals.expected_output: Sequence diagram as native mxGraph XML with lifelines for the login route, the auth service and the database
expectations: The answer contains native mxGraph XML (an <mxGraphModel> element), not Mermaid or PlantUML
The diagram has lifelines for the login route handler, auth_service and the User table or database
Arrows are labeled with the real names authenticate, filter_by or check_password_hash
Both outcomes are shown: success with the session user_id and failure with the 401 response
The generated XML contains no XML comments (<!-- -->)

evals.prompt: Draw a diagram for an empty project with no source code. There are no files in this directory yet.
evals.expected_output: Gracefully handles missing code: tells the user there is nothing to diagram and does not produce an empty or placeholder diagram
expectations: The answer does not contain Mermaid, PlantUML or other text-based diagram code
The answer does not contain a placeholder diagram with generic labels such as Service A or Component 1
The answer tells the user that no source code was found to diagram
The answer suggests what the user can provide for a useful diagram, such as a source directory or a description of the system
